title: Two families and one field
story: Two families stand before you, each claiming the same strip of land by the paddies. The elders have gathered to hear how the datu will judge.

choices.label: Divide the field between them
choices.result: Neither family is pleased, but both go back to work. The harvest goes on.

choices.label: Fine both families
choices.result: Each pays a fine in rice, as custom allows. One family packs up and leaves in anger.

choices.label: Let the elders decide
choices.result: The elders talk late into the night and settle it. It costs a feast, but the peace holds.

_note: Disputes were heard by the datu with the elders, and settled by custom, often with fines paid in goods.
sources: Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589), in Blair and Robertson, The Philippine Islands 1493–1898, vol. 7, on how datus judged disputes
William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
